simple.meaning: שֵׁד (shêd) is a Hebrew word meaning “a dæmon (as malignant ).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שֵׁד (H7700) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Deuteronomy 32:17, with occurrences in Deuteronomy, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שֵׁד (H7700) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שֵׁד (H7700) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שֵׁד (shêd) / H7700 is traced through Deuteronomy 32:17, Psalms 106:37 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7700. shed [ שֵׁד ] noun [masculine] apparently demon (loan-word from Assyrian šêdu , a protecting spirit, especially of bull-colossus, Dl Pa 153 f. ; WB 645 COT Deut 32:17 Zim KAT3. 460 f. , 455, 649; compare Aramaic שֵׁידָא , demon , and (perhaps) Phoenician proper name גדשד Nö ZMG xiii (1888), 481 Lzb 249 ; originally √ שׁוד ( = Arabic rule ) according to Thes Baud Semitic Rei. i. 130 ff. Dl WB and others; > Arabic (III, IV aid , Hom ZMG xlvi (1892), 529, against this Zim l. c ); — אֱלֹהַּ לֹא לַשֵּׁדִים יִזְבְּחוּ 32:17 (compare Dr), Psa 106:37 (human sacrifice).
